He is lying, and here is why, plainly and factually.

The year to date deficit comparison is misleading by design. Comparing partial year deficits without adjusting for timing effects is a classic budget trick. Large outlays and revenues do not occur evenly across the year. Shifts in tax filing dates, delayed appropriations, disaster funding, student loan flows, and trust fund transfers can move hundreds of billions from one fiscal window to another without changing the underlying trajectory. A smaller year to date number does not mean policy improvement, it usually means spending has been pushed later or revenues were pulled forward.

There is no evidence this change is caused by policy under the convicted felon. Deficits are driven by spending, revenue, and interest costs. Mandatory spending continues to rise, interest costs are exploding due to higher rates and accumulated debt, and there has been no structural spending reform. Without major legislative changes, claiming credit for a short term accounting shift is dishonest .

The deficit to GDP claim is also misleading. A lower ratio can occur simply because nominal GDP rises due to inflation, even while deficits remain historically large in absolute terms. Running a deficit equal to 5.5 percent, if that's true, of GDP is still very high by historical standards, especially outside of a recession or war. Calling 6.8 percent under Biden unsustainable while pretending 5.5 percent is suddenly healthy is arbitrary spin, not economics. And remember those ratios describe trend projections, not proof of improved fiscal health due to policy changes.

The claim that we will grow our way out of debt is contradicted by the math. With interest costs now one of the fastest growing line items in the federal budget, growth alone cannot offset deficits unless growth consistently exceeds interest rates and primary deficits are reduced. None of that is happening. Higher deficits paired with rate cuts signal economic weakness, not strength.

If government finances were truly improving, interest costs as a share of spending would be falling, not rising, and long term deficit projections would be improving, not worsening. They are doing the opposite.

This is not fiscal discipline. It is cherry picked timing data, ratio games, and political marketing, and it collapses the moment you look past the headline.
